discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Good catch — the code fixtures all carried "overloaded" in the message, so the code check was not covered on its own. Added table-driven cases for each capacity code with a neutral message, plus an unknown code with a neutral message that must stay non-retryable.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

I don't think this applies to marketplace skills. The exact directory/frontmatter match is enforced by `validateAgentSkillName` in `extensions/agent-plugin/agent-skill.ts`, which only runs for skills that come from an Agent Plugin package. Its docstring says Cline's own skill files intentionally stay more permissive. Skills under `~/.agents/skills` go through `createSkillsConfigDefinition` → `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown`, which uses the frontmatter name (falling back to the directory name) and keys the skill by that name, with no directory check.

You're right that the test only checked the directory, though. The `foo`/`bar` test now also loads the skills directory through `createUserInstructionConfigWatcher` and asserts the skill is registered as `bar` with its description, so it proves the installed skill actually loads and isn't just present on disk.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Valid, fixed. The reveal-only test now stubs `VscodeTerminalProcess.prototype.run` instead of handing the process a never-ending stream, so no shell-execution or terminal-close listeners outlive the test.

Added two cases: a `tool_call.id` given as a number, which checks the message names `tool_call.id`, and a payload missing four required fields, which checks exactly three are listed. Each one fails if I break the matching part of the formatting (joining the path, or the `slice(0, 3)` limit).

// `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` adapter (bedrock.test.ts mocks the constructor).
 // Each case streams one turn through the gateway with a stubbed fetch and
 // asserts on the `additionalModelRequestFields` the adapter put on the
-// Converse request. They pin the reason for the adapter floor of 5.0.65:
-// OpenAI models reached through inference profiles (`us.openai.*`,
-// `global.openai.*`) must get `reasoning.effort`, the field Bedrock accepts,
-// not the generic `reasoningConfig` that older adapters emitted for any id
-// they did not recognise (cline/cline#14451, vercel/ai#19403).
+// Converse request. Together they pin the adapter floor:
+//
+//   1. OpenAI models reached through inference profiles (`us.openai.*`,
+//      `global.openai.*`) get `reasoning.effort`, the field Bedrock accepts,
+//      not the generic `reasoningConfig` that adapters before 5.0.65 emitted
+//      for any id they did not recognise (cline/cline#14451, vercel/ai#19403);
+//   2. models the adapter cannot classify get no reasoning fields at all,
+//      instead of a `reasoningConfig` Bedrock rejects for models without
+//      reasoning support — adapters before 5.0.96 sent it for every
+//      non-Anthropic id (cline/cline#14095, vercel/ai#21487);
+//   3. the families the adapter does classify keep their native shapes from
+//      the id alone even when the catalog does not list the model, so a
+//      catalog that lags a model launch never switches thinking off.
+//
+// Cases that would only assert the adapter's translation for an id it
+// classifies belong to the adapter's own suite and are deliberately absent.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Intentional. That case exercised none of Cline's routing; it only pinned how `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` translates an id it classifies itself, which belongs to the adapter's own suite. The remaining cases pin what goes through Cline's resolver, catalog lookup and portable-reasoning path, and the live run in the PR body records Nova 2 Lite's accepted request shape.

Skipping this one. connect.test.ts has no WebSocket fixture today (it only covers resolveHubUrl), so testing the probe handler's parse path would mean building a fake socket harness for a guard that is five lines and mirrors the NodeHubClient one, which is covered. Not worth the added test scaffolding.

Valid — fixed, test-first: both `stop` and `max-tokens` empty retries reproduced exactly this (`Model returned empty response`, truncated turn gone). An empty retry is no more a replacement than an aborted or errored one, so it now keeps the truncated turn and lets the loop surface the max-tokens error, matching the nothing-to-compact path. Also added a table-driven test over the full retry-outcome matrix (every finish reason × text / tool call / empty / provider-executed activity) asserting the partial answer is never silently dropped and the loop is never handed an empty turn — all 20 cells pass.
